subject: Integration Qs: Auth, Routing & Dedicated Capacity for Atlas Analytics

Subject: Demo follow-up — integration & dedicated sizing questions

Hi Sana — thanks again for the demo window today. Quick recap + a focused set of questions to help our engineers size a Dedicated pool and draft an implementation runbook. Attaching a short overview (redwood-integration-overview.pdf).

Recap (2 min):
- Goal: embed LLM features into search & assisted workflows (query generation + reranking + structured tool-calls).
- Target SLOs: 95th pct latency < 400ms for single-turn generation in interactive UI; background batch jobs can be slower.
- Expected traffic profile (rough): mostly small queries with medium-length context + occasional long prompt in export jobs.

Open questions we need answered to recommend Dedicated sizing and routing:
1) Steady-state QPS and peak spikes you expect (include percent of requests that require reranking vs simple generation).
2) Typical token distribution (prompt + response average tokens).
3) Embeddings footprint: number of docs, update cadence, whether you want on-the-fly embedding or precompute -> re-ranker design.
4) Auth model: will Atlas use a single service token per app or per-end-user tokens? Any KMS/HSM requirements?
5) Routing policy preferences: strict region pinning, latency-first, or cost-first fallback rules?

What we'll deliver after we get answers:
- Recommended Dedicated pool configuration (GPU count/type), concurrency limits, autoscaling policy (queue depth/latency triggers), and warmup guidance.
- Suggested SDK/auth examples for your engineers (node/python snippets) and a small sample for structured output / function-calling enforcement.
- A one-hour technical sync with Aditya + Marcus to walk the config and runtime tradeoffs.

Proposed next step: technical sync Wed 2026-07-14 10:00 AM PT — does that work for you? Calendar: https://calendly.com/rachel-k/atlas-technical-sync

Thanks,
Rachel Kim

Hi Rachel — great summary, thanks. Answers inline below. Attaching our latency SLO doc for reference (atlas_latency_slo.pdf).

1) Traffic: steady-state ~120 req/s for the main product API (user-facing), with predictable business-hours spikes up to 400 req/s (10–15 minute bursts). About ~20% of requests will include a reranker step (candidate generator -> top-10 rerank). Background export jobs run overnight at much higher token counts but are not latency-sensitive.

2) Tokens: average prompt + response ~350 tokens for interactive flows; short queries ~100 tokens. Heavy export jobs average 4k tokens.

3) Embeddings: corpus ~250K documents, we prefer precomputed vectors for search (updates nightly), but we may also want on-the-fly embedding for short user annotations. Reranker will run on top-10 candidates (embedding used to produce candidate list; rerank uses full-context generation).

4) Auth: we plan to use a single service account token per environment (staging/prod) with HSM-backed keys for signing. We will need audit logs tied to each token.

5) Routing: latency-first within region (US), with a cost-fallback to lower-tier model outside business hours. Region pinning required for data residency on a per-environment basis.

Let us know if you need more detail on document sizes or update cadence. Wed 7/14 10am PT works — I've added the slot.

Thanks,
Sana Patel
Director of Product | Atlas Analytics

Hi Sana — looping in a few technical recommendations based on the numbers you shared. I'm copying some pragmatic configs you can use as a starting point and what we'll cover on the sync.

Short answers / sizing guidance:
- Start with a Dedicated pool sized for ~2x steady-state throughput to handle normal burst smoothing (so for 120 steady -> plan for capacity to handle ~240 sustained equivalent). Given your spike profile (up to 400 short bursts), we recommend burst capacity via autoscale instead of permanently provisioning to 400.
- GPU baseline: 2 x 80GB A100-equivalent nodes (or equivalent mixture of T4s + A10s if cost sensitive) is a reasonable starting point. These nodes give headroom for batching and rerank workflows.
- Concurrency: set per-instance concurrency_limit = 10 for generation endpoints that handle ~350 tokens average. For short/query endpoints (100 tokens avg) you can set concurrency_limit = 20. These values help avoid OOM and keep latencies predictable.
- Batching: enable adaptive batching with a target max_batch_size = 32 and a latency cap of 150ms for interactive endpoints. This preserves latency SLO while improving token throughput.
- Reranker pattern: candidate generation on a smaller model (cheaper) -> embed candidates -> rerank top-10 on dedicated rerank endpoint. Consider running rerank on CPU-backed instances if the model is small; otherwise dedicate 1 GPU per N concurrent rerank requests.
- Embeddings: precompute nightly for the 250K corpus and serve from a vector DB. For on-the-fly small embeddings (annotations), route to a separate embedding endpoint with lower concurrency limits to avoid contention.

Autoscaling / queueing strategy:
- Autoscale trigger: use queue_depth (requests waiting) + 95th latency crossing threshold as a composite metric. Example policy: scale up +1 instance when queue_depth > 100 OR p95_latency > 400ms for 2 minutes; scale down if queue_depth < 20 and p95_latency < 200ms for 10 minutes.
- Warmup: keep a 10% buffer of warm instances during business hours to avoid cold-start latency; for scheduled heavy exports, allow scheduled scale-up windows.
- Queues: implement a front-door queue with request categorization (interactive vs background vs batch). Prioritize interactive and apply token-based throttling on background jobs. We recommend circuit-breaker rules for sustained overload (reject at 429 with Retry-After header).

Auth & audit:
- Service tokens per environment + HSM for signing matches our recommended pattern. Redwood can push token usage logs and per-token audit events to your SIEM via the private deployment connector (we'll show the schema on the call).

SDK & routing notes:
- SDK: use Redwood SDK for auth (service-token flow) and automatic retry/backoff. We'll provide node/python snippets.
- Routing: configure a policy that pins region=us for prod, fallback to a lower-cost model only outside business hours. Use model-variant tags so the runtime can fallback automatically when capacity is constrained.

Example config excerpt (pseudo-CLI):

  create-dedicated-pool --name atlas-prod-pool --gpu-type a100-80 --min-instances 2 --max-instances 6 --concurrency-limit 10 --batching adaptive --max-batch-size 32 --scale-policy "queue_depth>100:scale_up:1"

What we'll bring to the sync:
- A suggested pool config file you can import into your infra team (YAML).
- Node/Python SDK snippets for service-token auth, function-calling examples, and structured-output schema enforcement.
- A short checklist for embedding ops (vector DB snapshot cadence, rebuild windows, memory/pinned-index sizing).

If that matches expectations we can convert the recommendations into an initial CI configuration and a canary rollout plan for the first week.

Cheers,
Aditya Rao
Solutions Engineering Lead | Redwood Inference
